comments.author: @horrorislander
comments.text: I've been spending the last few weeks learning python with the help of AI. I used to be a software engineer, but mostly embedded systems, meaning I started out "rolling my own" for everything, only slowly using the occasional library or "os" as such things built on in that space. In short, I'm not a master of the myriad libraries that python and other user-oriented environments are always filled with, so having a tool like the various LLMs that do know all these modules has been very helpful to me. This is what I thought about when imagining a "gold medal"-level math AI. I'm not particularly shaken by the idea of AIs being better at math than humans, since almost all interesting proofs have always been generated by someone somewhere else in time and space who bequeathed me their results. But I am much more excited by the notion of an assistant that can understand the problems that interest me and knows all the existing solutions that may apply, and can either serve those up (or even explain them) to me, as well as recognize new problems that it can work on solving. Math is far too large for any one human to know what exists, much less what is possible, so just as LLMs help me navigate python modules, such an AI would be a wonderful help in navigating math.

comments.author: @ewallt
comments.text:
Regarding AlphaGo, there were some errors. One is Lee Sedol was not the world champion at the time of the match. He was a former world champion. Still a top player, but there were others who were better. Regarding move 37, it wasn’t a move that people laughed at or thought was weak, but it was indeed startling. It was a shoulder hit on the 5th line, which is considered bad because it gives away too much territory. A commentator thought there may have been a transcription error. It wasn’t a winning move, however, but a very good one among other equally good alternatives, but what made it stand out was it was a move that no hums would make.

At this point, the AI was still relying heavily on human moves which it had in a database. Google would later rewrite it so that it learned only by playing itself, but that wasn’t this version, which makes it even more reliable it was able to come up with a move like that.

There was another similar type move, but not as startling, where the commentators said “If this is a good move, this program is a lot better than I am.”

comments.author: @i2c_jason
comments.text: Very few people seem to realize the step function we'll see when math and geometry are accurately imagined by AI. This has been the sole impediment to, for example, prompting ChatGPT to return an accurate 3D STEP file. Or, better yet, prompting for a 3D STEP assembly. As soon as this can be done, engineering and manufacturing will be changed forever. In my estimation, this step change across industry will be something like this: Industrial designers are not needed any more, as the engineer will be able to craft and iterate prompts to acheive their ends (and vice versa, designers can prompt away the engineer). Prototyping and manufacturing will then be within striking distance of a single prompt. I can imagine a marketplace or wrapper website where you prompt your product and prototypes show up at your door. Once the STEP file assembly can be imagined, then it can be simulated and tested by other agents, 2D drawings made by agents, BOM created and sourced by agents, and parts ordered by an agent. This brings me to what I've been saying since 2022 - the only safe place when this creativity and abundance wave hits will be to run your own physical factory supplying all of these widgets and parts to anyone with a prompt input to an AI. It's going to be a wild ride. I talk about all of this on my TikTok from the perspective of an electrical engineer at i2c_jason.

comments.text:
"AI" is completely fine, but labeling it with human-only characteristics "intelligence", "sentience", "reasoning", etc. is seriously not a good idea

I mean to say this as a warning, and not an ego-filled rant:

The One God Hates those who imitate the ability to create animate beings.

LLM's are fine and using statistical models are fine, but acting as if a bunch of 1s and 0s suddenly leapt into a whole different categorical domain outside of simply being binary combinations of energy on a computer, is both illogical (no combination of blue paint can ever turn into red paint, purely by virtue of the combination) and arrogant (to think that we are now the Creator-s and not just the create-d)

Please consider refraining from labeling literal computer programs with human qualities (qualities that transcend binary configurations and combinations of atoms)

Instead use phrases like "text output" instead of "it said"

And not "i'm talking to it" but "i'm querying it"

just because there are varied outputs, doesn't mean that the outputs still aren't results of purely binary and mathematical operations like any other program
